Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Plan targets current physical health issue; no discrete mental-health problem identified.)

Principal Problem: Acute asthma exacerbation
- Patient Goal(s): Regain normal breathing, return to running without SOB  
- Clinical Goal(s): Stabilize respiratory status; optimize inhaler regimen; review within days  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Increase Clenil to 4 puffs BID as instructed  
  • Use Salbutamol up to every 2–4 h PRN; seek A&E if symptoms worsen  
  • Book face-to-face GP review/peak-flow check within next few days  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Schedule urgent asthma review with examination and peak-flow measurement  
  • Assess need for oral steroids/antibiotics at review  
  • Provide inhaler-technique education; supply written asthma action plan  

Secondary Problem: Atopy (hay fever / possible eczema)
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce skin irritation and allergic symptoms  
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm eczema diagnosis; manage seasonal allergies effectively  
- Actions (Patient): Continue topical treatments as prescribed; monitor triggers  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Review dermatological symptoms at next visit; consider antihistamine or stronger topical therapy if needed  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Inhaler dosing, action plan for worsening symptoms, A&E indicators  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased use of Salbutamol, declining peak-flow, nocturnal SOB, inability to speak in full sentences  
- Coping Strategies: Follow written asthma plan; maintain routine peak-flow monitoring; avoid known triggers

- Asthma exacerbation – High likelihood: Established asthma with new wheeze/SOB; poor reliever response  
- Viral URTI triggering asthma – Medium likelihood: Abrupt onset over 2–3 days; cough present without systemic signs  
- Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction / inhaler technique issues – Medium likelihood: Symptoms began during running; may reflect sub-optimal preventer use
